title: Channels of Distribution

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Mark (W) for wholesaler or (R) for retailer: (a) Dealing in a limited range of goods only (b) Direct contact with consumers.
questions.answer:
(a) W — a wholesaler deals in one line of goods.
(b) R — a retailer deals directly with consumers.

questions.q: Mark (W) for wholesaler or (R) for retailer: (a) Selling goods in small quantities (b) More capital required.
Dalmia Oil Mills produces refined oil; Ruchi Oil Depot lifts its entire production and sells to retailers; Mrs. Priti buys 2 litres from Balaji Groceries. Name the (a) retailer (b) wholesaler.
questions.answer:
(a) Balaji Groceries
(b) Ruchi Oil Depot
(Dalmia Oil Mills is the manufacturer and Mrs. Priti the consumer.)

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) A channel of distribution is the path by which goods and services travel to the intended consumer. (b) The retailer is the channel member who deals with the final consumer.
Fill in the blanks: (a) ________ represents the chain of intermediaries through which the final buyer purchases goods. (b) A wholesaler is a link between the manufacturer and the ________.
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Wholesalers require a small amount of capital. (b) A channel of distribution is the route taken by goods from producers to consumers.
questions.answer:
(a) False — they need a large amount of capital.
(b) True

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) A wholesaler is an important link between the producer and the ________. (b) A retailer acts as a ________ between the wholesaler and the ultimate consumer.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What risks are borne by retailers? Mention any two.
questions.answer:
(1) Loss of goods by fire or theft.
(2) Deterioration in quality of goods while they remain unsold.
(3) Change in fashion and taste of consumers, leaving goods unsold. (Any two.)

questions.q: A publisher sells books to a wholesaler who sells to local bookstores. Name the channel and the role of the wholesaler.
questions.answer:
Channel: Producer (publisher) → Wholesaler → Retailer (bookstores) → Consumer — an indirect, two-level channel.
The wholesaler buys in bulk, stores the books and distributes them in smaller lots to bookstores, often on credit.

or.q: How do retailers help in stabilising prices?
or.answer: Retailers keep stocks and buy regularly from wholesalers, so goods are available steadily; by informing wholesalers about demand they help match supply with demand, which keeps prices stable.

questions.q: State any two functions of a retailer.
questions.answer:
(1) Buying and assembling a variety of goods from many suppliers.
(2) Personal service — advice and home delivery; also credit to regular customers, display and storage of goods.

or.q: What is a direct channel? Give two examples.
or.answer: A channel in which the producer sells directly to the consumer without any middleman. Examples: Bata selling through its own shops; banking, insurance and telephone services; door-to-door selling.

questions.q: Explain two functions of wholesalers.
questions.answer:
(1) Storage — they store goods in warehouses until retailers need them.
(2) Financing — they give advances to producers and credit to retailers.
(Also: collection, distribution, risk bearing, grading, pricing.)

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of retailers in the distribution of goods.
questions.answer:
(1) They buy and assemble goods from many wholesalers and producers and make them available near consumers.
(2) They sell in small quantities, saving consumers from storing goods.
(3) They give credit, advice and home delivery.
(4) They pass on information about consumers' tastes to producers and help introduce new products.

questions.q: How do retailers help consumers? Give any three ways.
questions.answer:
(1) Regular supply of a variety of goods near the home, in small quantities.
(2) Personal service — guidance on quality and use, home delivery and credit facility.
(3) Attractive display and information about new products, helping consumers choose.

or.q: Mention any three differences between wholesalers and retailers.
or.answer:
Quantity: wholesalers deal in bulk; retailers in small quantities.
Capital: wholesalers need more; retailers less.
Contact with consumers: wholesalers have none; retailers have direct contact.

questions.q: State any three differences between wholesalers and retailers.
questions.answer:
(1) Buying: wholesalers buy from producers in bulk; retailers buy from wholesalers in small quantities.
(2) Variety: wholesalers deal in a limited line; retailers in a wide range.
(3) Purpose of sale: wholesalers sell for resale; retailers sell for consumption.

questions.q: Define retailers and state any three of their functions.
questions.answer:
Retailers are traders who buy goods from wholesalers or producers and sell them in small quantities to final consumers.
Functions: buying and assembling goods; storage; credit and personal services; risk bearing; display; supply of information.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is a channel of distribution? Explain the various types of channels.
questions.answer:
A channel of distribution is the route along which goods move from the producer to the final consumer, through middlemen if needed.
Direct channel: Producer → Consumer — through the producer's own shops, door-to-door salesmen, mail order; used for services and heavy equipment.
Indirect channels: (1) Producer → Retailer → Consumer — for big retailers and local goods; (2) Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer — the common channel for consumer goods; (3) Producer → Agent → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer — long channel for goods sold over wide areas; (4) Producer → Agent → Consumer; (5) Producer → Wholesaler → Consumer.

questions.q: What is meant by channels of distribution? Explain any four services distributed through the direct channel, with examples.
questions.answer:
A channel of distribution is the path by which goods and services reach consumers from producers.
Services are produced and consumed at the same time, so they are distributed directly:
(1) Banking — the bank serves customers at its branches and online (SBI).
(2) Insurance — the company or its own agents issue policies (LIC).
(3) Transport — railways, airlines and buses carry passengers directly.
(4) Telephone and Internet services (BSNL, Airtel).
(5) Medical, legal, education and consultancy services.

questions.q: Explain any five functions of retailers.
questions.answer:
(1) Buying and assembling goods of many brands and varieties.
(2) Storage — keeping stock so consumers can buy any time.
(3) Credit facility to regular customers.
(4) Personal services — advice, after-sales help and home delivery.
(5) Risk bearing — fire, theft, spoilage, change in fashion.
(6) Display and supply of information to producers.

questions.q: State any four functions of a wholesaler.
questions.answer:
(1) Collection of goods in bulk from producers.
(2) Storage until goods are sold.
(3) Distribution to retailers.
(4) Financing producers (advances) and retailers (credit).
(5) Risk bearing, grading and packing, and stabilising prices.

questions.q: State any six differences between wholesalers and retailers.
questions.answer:
(1) Quantity — bulk vs small.
(2) Buy from — producers vs wholesalers.
(3) Variety — limited line vs wide range.
(4) Capital — more vs less.
(5) Sale — for resale vs for consumption.
(6) Contact with consumers — none vs direct.
(7) Decoration of shop — little vs much.
